title: UNIT 5: CHALLENGES OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Economic development → a process of improving people's living standards through increases in income, employment, production, access to basic services, and overall well-being.

Challenges of economic development → conditions that slow down or prevent improvements in people's living standards and the sustainable development of countries.

title: 5.1 MULTIPLE FACES OF POVERTY AND IMPLICATION TO DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Poverty → a condition in which people lack sufficient resources and opportunities to meet their basic needs and achieve an acceptable standard of living.

◆ MULTIPLE FACES OF POVERTY
✓ Income poverty → lack of sufficient income or purchasing power to meet basic needs.
✓ Food poverty → inadequate access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food.
✓ Health poverty → lack of adequate health services, medicines, sanitation and clean water.
✓ Educational poverty → limited access to quality education and learning opportunities.
✓ Housing poverty → lack of safe, adequate and affordable housing.
✓ Employment poverty → lack of decent, productive and adequately paid employment.
✓ Social poverty → exclusion from social, economic and political opportunities.
✓ Environmental poverty → dependence on degraded natural resources and exposure to environmental problems.

◆ CAUSES OF POVERTY
✓ Unemployment and underemployment.
✓ Low productivity and low income.
✓ Rapid population growth.
✓ Limited access to education and health services.
✓ Unequal distribution of resources and income.
✓ Environmental degradation and natural disasters.
✓ Conflict and political instability.
✓ Limited infrastructure and investment.

◆ IMPLICATIONS OF POVERTY FOR DEVELOPMENT
✓ Reduces people's ability to invest in education and health.
✓ Increases malnutrition and disease.
✓ Reduces labour productivity.
✓ Increases unemployment and dependency.
✓ Limits access to productive resources and opportunities.
✓ Can increase social inequality and exclusion.
✓ May contribute to environmental degradation as people depend heavily on natural resources.
✓ Slows economic growth and human development.

Poverty and underdevelopment can reinforce each other: poverty reduces opportunities for development, while limited development can create conditions that keep people in poverty.

title: 5.2 THE ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES OF GLOBALIZATION
notes:
Globalization → the increasing interaction and integration of people, economies, cultures and institutions across countries through trade, investment, technology, communication and movement of people.

◆ ADVANTAGES OF GLOBALIZATION
✓ Expands international trade and markets.
✓ Increases access to goods, services and technologies.
✓ Encourages foreign investment.
✓ Creates opportunities for employment and business.
✓ Facilitates the transfer of knowledge, skills and technology.
✓ Improves communication and access to information.
✓ Can increase competition and encourage better products and services.
✓ Promotes cultural exchange and international cooperation.
✓ Can support economic growth and development.

◆ DISADVANTAGES OF GLOBALIZATION
✓ Can increase inequality within and between countries.
✓ Local industries may face strong competition from foreign companies.
✓ Poor countries may become dependent on external markets, investment and technology.
✓ Economic problems in one country can spread to other countries.
✓ May contribute to exploitation of labour and natural resources.
✓ Can increase environmental degradation when production expands without proper controls.
✓ Local cultures and traditions may be weakened by cultural influences from abroad.
✓ Benefits may be distributed unevenly among people and regions.

Globalization has both positive and negative effects. Its contribution to development depends on how countries manage trade, investment, technology, labour and natural resources.

title: 5.3 THE GROWING IMBALANCE BETWEEN REGIONS AND COUNTRIES
notes:
Regional and international imbalance → differences in economic development, income, access to services, infrastructure and opportunities among regions within a country and among different countries.

◆ FORMS OF IMBALANCE
✓ Income inequality → large differences in income and wealth among people and regions.
✓ Development inequality → differences in economic and social development.
✓ Infrastructure inequality → unequal access to roads, electricity, water, communication and other facilities.
✓ Educational inequality → unequal access to schools, teachers and educational opportunities.
✓ Health inequality → differences in access to hospitals, health workers, medicines and sanitation.
✓ Employment inequality → differences in availability of productive and decent jobs.

◆ CAUSES
✓ Unequal distribution of natural resources.
✓ Differences in infrastructure and investment.
✓ Unequal access to education and technology.
✓ Historical differences in economic development.
✓ Differences in government policies and institutions.
✓ Unequal participation in international trade.
✓ Conflict and political instability.
✓ Differences in human capital and productivity.
✓ Geographical and environmental conditions.

◆ IMPLICATIONS
✓ Increases poverty and inequality.
✓ Encourages migration from less-developed to more-developed areas.
✓ Creates unequal access to basic services.
✓ Can increase social and political tensions.
✓ Limits balanced national development.
✓ May increase dependence of poorer countries on richer countries.

Balanced development requires investment in disadvantaged regions, improved infrastructure, quality education and health services, employment opportunities, and fair access to economic resources.

title: 5.4 CORRUPTION
notes:
Corruption → the misuse of entrusted power or position for private or personal benefit.

◆ COMMON FORMS OF CORRUPTION
✓ Bribery → giving or receiving money, gifts or other benefits to influence a decision or action.
✓ Embezzlement → illegally taking or using money or property entrusted to a person.
✓ Nepotism → giving jobs or opportunities to relatives or close associates unfairly.
✓ Fraud → deliberate deception for financial or other personal gain.
✓ Abuse of power → using official authority for improper personal benefit.
✓ Favoritism → giving unfair advantages to particular people or groups.

◆ CAUSES OF CORRUPTION
✓ Weak institutions and law enforcement.
✓ Lack of transparency and accountability.
✓ Abuse of political or administrative power.
✓ Poor control over public resources.
✓ Lack of effective monitoring.
✓ Opportunities for personal gain.
✓ Weak ethical standards.

◆ EFFECTS OF CORRUPTION ON DEVELOPMENT
✓ Diverts public resources from development projects.
✓ Increases the cost of public services and projects.
✓ Reduces government revenue.
✓ Discourages domestic and foreign investment.
✓ Reduces public trust in institutions.
✓ Weakens the quality of public services.
✓ Increases inequality and unfair access to opportunities.
✓ Slows economic growth and development.
✓ Can encourage further illegal practices.

◆ MEASURES TO REDUCE CORRUPTION
✓ Strengthening laws and institutions.
✓ Improving transparency and accountability.
✓ Effective auditing and monitoring of public resources.
✓ Promoting ethical behaviour and public awareness.
✓ Ensuring equal application of laws.
✓ Protecting systems for reporting corruption.
✓ Increasing citizen participation and oversight.

title: 5.5 GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
notes:
Global health crisis → a serious health threat that affects large populations and may spread across countries or regions, requiring coordinated national and international responses.

◆ EXAMPLES OF GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
✓ Infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics.
✓ HIV/AIDS.
✓ COVID-19.
✓ Malaria and other major communicable diseases.
✓ Antimicrobial resistance.
✓ Other health emergencies that cross national borders.

◆ FACTORS THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
✓ International travel and movement of people.
✓ Rapid urbanization and population growth.
✓ Poor sanitation and limited access to clean water.
✓ Weak health systems.
✓ Poverty and malnutrition.
✓ Environmental changes and habitat disruption.
✓ Limited access to medicines and health technologies.
✓ Inadequate disease surveillance and preparedness.

◆ EFFECTS ON ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
✓ Increases illness and death.
✓ Reduces labour productivity.
✓ Increases household and government health expenditure.
✓ Disrupts education and employment.
✓ Reduces production and economic activity.
✓ Disrupts trade, transport and tourism.
✓ Can increase poverty and inequality.
✓ Places additional pressure on health systems and public resources.

◆ MEASURES TO ADDRESS GLOBAL HEALTH CRISES
✓ Strengthening health systems and health infrastructure.
✓ Improving disease surveillance and early warning systems.
✓ Providing vaccination and appropriate preventive measures.
✓ Improving sanitation, hygiene and access to clean water.
✓ Increasing public health education and awareness.
✓ Ensuring access to essential medicines and health technologies.
✓ Promoting national and international cooperation.
✓ Preparing emergency response systems before crises occur.

Global health crises are development challenges because they affect human health, labour productivity, education, household income and economic activities at local, national and international levels.
